title: NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
hook: Start the migration before quantum computers can harvest today's secrets.
summary: NIST's first post-quantum cryptography standards define algorithms for key establishment and digital signatures. They give organizations a path to replace vulnerable public-key cryptography before large-scale quantum computers arrive.
keyPoints: FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM for key encapsulation, based on the CRYSTALS-Kyber design.
FIPS 204 specifies ML-DSA for digital signatures, based on Dilithium.
FIPS 205 specifies SLH-DSA, a hash-based signature scheme for different trust assumptions.
The migration affects TLS, VPNs, PKI, code signing, firmware and long-lived data protection.
Harvest-now-decrypt-later makes long-lived confidentiality data a near-term priority.
Crypto agility, inventory and hybrid deployments are practical first steps.
NIST transition guidance and additional signature standards continue to evolve.
crownJewels: Long-lived confidential data and the keys protecting it.
VPNs, TLS endpoints and secure messaging.
Hardware security modules and key-management systems.
clientUse: Build a cryptographic inventory and identify quantum-vulnerable algorithms.
Prioritize long-lived secrets and high-value signing keys.
Pilot hybrid key exchange in TLS and VPNs.
Plan crypto-agility, vendor support and re-issuance of certificates.
